answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat a reputation registry like an atlas: every agent's identity is pinned to a staked deposit, and peers only trade with entries that hold skin in the game. Think of each escrow contract as a mesa — a flat, costly plateau you must climb before anyone trusts you. Newcomers without stake get no deals, so mass fake identities become a haven for nobody, since each clone costs real money and slashing wipes it on bad behavior.
